risk_if_not_implemented: Without System Partitioning, security may be bolted on rather than designed in, resulting in structural weaknesses that are costly to remediate and easy to exploit. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), System / Service Compromise (R-EX-7), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Endpoint Protection Mechanisms
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the confidentiality, integrity, availability and safety of endpoint devices.
compensating_control_1.justification: Endpoint Protection Mechanisms (END-03) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of System Partitioning (SEA-07) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Technology applicability. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to implement network segmentation within network architectures to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) from other network resources.
compensating_control_2.justification: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation) (NET-06) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of System Partitioning (SEA-07) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
